earlier_scan.source_named: Fransen, Margo A. E. 1995. A Grammar of Limbum: a Grassfields Bantu Language spoken in the North-West Province of Cameroon. PhD, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
earlier_scan.note: Long grammar with phonology; no open copy found (VU portal search empty). Tonal Grassfields Bantu; also Nforgwei 2004, Ndi 2019.

sources.citation: Tabah Nforgwei, Samuel. 2004. A Study of the Phonological, Morphological and Syntactic Processes in the Standardisation of Limbum. PhD thesis, Université de Yaoundé I. 440 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No occurrence of stress/accent/prominence in the prosodic sense anywhere in the 440-page text layer. Ch. 2 (pp. 48-88) covers syllable structure of the three dialects, word structure by syllable count, phonological processes, and tone marking (3 level tones, 5 contours, citing Fiore 1987:119, Fransen 1995:73, Mfonyam 1989).

sources.citation: Bradley, Virginia. 1994. Description of Surface Tone in the Limbum Verb Phrase. SIL Cameroon. 12 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone only: 3 level tones H M L plus 5 glides; 'the great majority of Limbum words are monosyllabic'; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Fiore, Lynne E. 1977. A Phonology of Limbum (Nsungli). Yaoundé: SIL / CE.RE.L.TRA, ONAREST. 111 pp. (central/Wat dialect)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Ch. 5 Tone (p. 77): tone is a suprasegmental phoneme, every syllable carries tone, 7 contrastive tones on non-verbal stems, 2 on verb stems; ch. 6 describes clause-final decrescendo only; ch. 2 (p. 8) says the phonological word was not studied.

sources.citation: Mpoche, Kizitus Nformi. 1993. The Limbum noun phrase (a generative approach). MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé. 85 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syntax only; brief mention of tone marking conventions; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mfonyam, Joseph Ngwa. 1989. Tone in Orthography: The Case of Bafut and Related Languages. PhD thesis, Université de Yaoundé. xvi+686 pp. (ch. 26 'Limbum tone system', pp. 434ff.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Limbum chapter: three phonemic level tones H, M, L and five contour tones; no statement about stress in Limbum (its only 'stress accent' remark is that Mankon 'does not seem to be a stress accent language', p. ~303).
States Limbum is a tone language (baa with six tonal meanings); does not discuss stress. Supplied the working URLs for Fiore 1977 and the MPI PuRe copies of Nforgwei 2004 and Mpoche 1993.
